Wendy’s Rejects Trian’s $1.4 Billion Takeover Offer

Company backs its own turnaround bid instead of being taken private by Nelson Peltz’s hedge fund

By

Wendy’s WEN -1.92 % decrease; down pointing triangle has rejected an unsolicited $1.4 billion bid led by Nelson Peltz’s Trian Fund Management to buy the struggling burger chain, and adopted policies to protect the chain from further hostile takeover attempts.

The Ohio-based restaurant chain said Thursday that its board had unanimously rejected the investor group’s offer last week to buy out the company for $7.35 a share in cash. The company’s board said it is confident in new Chief Executive Bob Wright and his turnaround strategy, which is showing some early results. It also said the Trian proposal undervalues the company.
